subject.title: [Feature]: Global (IP-agnostic) auth rate limiting option for public-exposed deployments

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in IP-agnostic failed-auth lockout mode to `gateway.auth.rateLimit` for public-exposed shared-secret deployments?
rationale: The per-IP behavior is real, but choosing a global bucket changes the Gateway auth security boundary and can intentionally lock out legitimate clients during a distributed attack.

options.title: Add opt-in keying mode
options.body: Add a default-off global or named keying mode with config schema, docs, audit wording, and focused HTTP/WS coverage while preserving current per-IP defaults.

options.title: Keep current guidance
options.body: Decline the new knob and steer public deployments toward identity-aware proxy auth, strong secrets, firewall allowlists, and existing per-IP throttling.

options.title: Split password audit follow-up
options.body: Track password-length audit hardening separately so it does not block the rate-limit keying decision.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in keying mode
recommendation.body: Add a default-off global or named keying mode with config schema, docs, audit wording, and focused HTTP/WS coverage while preserving current per-IP defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a Gateway auth security/config policy decision, and steipete merged the original and adjacent auth rate-limit hardening work.
